C01.signature: Workers stage usable ordered covers before further cutting, compare target/cut/sewn dimensions and size-linked residuals, then revise supported allowances. Repeatable error despite accurate execution and reduced later resewing distinguish allowance error from worker/cloth variation. Requires representative pilots, measurement resolution and compliant layouts; wash measurements test a rival cause.
C01.reason: All 15 members explicitly test common-allowance error through early dimensional feedback; their replication and wash variants are compatible, without requiring customer-geometry transfer. F01/F02 supply correction and sequencing; F05/F06 supply diagnostics. F03 is not a shared operation here. C08 remains an uncertain link, not an automatic merge. Archive equivalence is local; no world outcome is tested.

C02.signature: Workers compare customer and reference placement using actual dimensions and corner profiles; corner-local failure at matched dimensions distinguishes geometry from nominal-size mismatch. Requires informative comparable measurements.
C02.reason: Preserve the agreed family: every member compares actual versus nominal dimensions and corner-related placement at comparable dimensions. Thickness, observation timing and access caveats refine the same diagnostic relation; they do not supply a separate causal intervention.

C03.signature: Workers measure seam-induced drift and manipulate feed direction or midpoint alignment on matched material; accurate cuts followed by length-dependent distortion that responds to seam technique implicate sewing. Requires representative strips and harmless marks.
C03.reason: Preserve the agreed family: both proposals locate distortion after sewing and intervene on feed/sequence while matching material and execution conditions. Midpoint alignment and feed reversal test the same hypothesized accumulation, with distinct but compatible observable responses. Strip-to-cover transfer remains untested.

C04.signature: Workers alter fixed pocket seam paths or internal folds to match measured corners while retaining panel/design; better rounded-corner seating at matched dimensions tests localized geometry correction. Requires sufficient existing allowance.
C04.reason: Preserve the agreed family: measured-corner pockets and alternative fixed seam/fold paths change local capture geometry while holding the printed panel and table dimensions. Both predict improved rounded seating and require enough allowance plus wash-stable construction; they implement archived revised pockets.

C05.signature: Workers combine actual-table geometry records with staged allowance calibration in cutting/pocket cards, comparing component-only and combined mockups before production. Accurate target geometry and calibrated construction jointly prevent fit mismatch; comparable assemblies and transferable measurements are assumed. All predict combined benefit; P012 additionally predicts a larger geometry effect under calibrated allowance.
C05.reason: The shared disputed kind is hypothesis because the added claim is a speculative joint-fit effect. Preserve the agreed three-member family and local novelty: each tests the same two inputs at the same cutting interface. P012 has a stronger interaction discriminator; P002/P003 outperforming either component alone cannot establish superadditivity. No interaction outcome is observed.

C06.signature: Workers add concealed washable elastic to corner pockets; local yielding accommodates radius differences at equal panel dimensions without puckering, slack or design shift. Requires suitable elastic and representative trials.
C06.reason: Preserve the agreed family: bridges, gathering and enclosed elastic all introduce local yielding at fixed panel dimensions, predicting rounded-corner seating without slack or print distortion. Their material, tension and access requirements remain candidate-specific; constructions are pairwise-compatible variants of archived compliance.

C07.signature: Workers measure both axes across cutting, sewing and washing at matched sizes; error onset and fixed versus percentage scaling distinguish construction uptake from proportional material change. Requires matched orders and adequate resolution.
C07.reason: Preserve the agreed singleton question and local novelty: onset across cutting/sewing/washing combined with fixed-versus-percentage error supplies the diagnostic discriminator. Required matched ordered designs and measurement resolution are unconfirmed, so the probe fit remains uncertain.

C08.signature: Workers calibrate a geometry-to-pattern rule using dimensions, corners, direction and wash change, then test withheld geometry before cutting similar orders. Requires reproducible geometry and transferable pilots.
C08.reason: The explicit claim is a speculative geometry-to-pattern transfer rule tested on withheld geometry. Archived calibration, early feedback, geometry measurement and wash measurement explain its agreed equivalent novelty. The actual rule is unspecified: the text cannot establish whether it reduces to C01 size-residual correction or changes the transfer relation. Keep separate with symmetric uncertainty; withholding alone proves neither distinction nor equivalence.

C09.signature: Workers temporarily release pockets and compare straight-edge fit; persistent shortfall implicates panel deficit, whereas release-only improvement implicates corner capture. Requires nondamaging temporary stitching.
C09.reason: Preserve question and new novelty. Temporarily releasing only pockets distinguishes a persistent panel deficit from local capture. F04/F05 are related retention/diagnostic baselines; F01 changes size-specific cutting allowances, an operation absent here. The supplied archive does not contain this release intervention.

C10.signature: Workers preset a concealed pleated pocket with a washable cloth tie for measured geometry; repeated placement and washing should preserve seating without resetting or tie drift. Requires cloth reserve and customer access.
C10.reason: Preserve the agreed singleton mechanism and parameter novelty: a preset pleat and cloth tie specialize adjustable corner retention. Seating without resetting and tie drift are implementation checks, not evidence of a further causal mechanism; cloth reserve and customer test access remain unknown.

C11.signature: Workers cross two-axis wash compensation with grain/print-constrained layout selection, comparing current or fixed-layout candidates with joint candidates before cutting. The hypothesis predicts maintained washed fit together with acceptable or reduced area waste. Representative offcuts and permissible alternative layouts are assumed; unsuitable orientation or excessive waste rejects a candidate.
C11.reason: Both members predict a speculative joint fit/yield advantage from the same compensation-layout coupling; classify that added claim as hypothesis. Preserve agreed new novelty. F06 supplies wash measurement; F01 calibrates size allowances on reference tables rather than directional compensation/layout selection, so exclude that match. Paper rejection gates do not establish a feasible production layout.
